subject: Local storage modes & TTL — customer Q&A and roadmap ask
messages:
From: Alicia Barnes <alicia.barnes@acme-corp.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-21T14:02:00Z
Subject: Questions on regional storage modes + configurable TTL for PII data

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Thank you for the walkthrough earlier. Two quick follow-ups from our security and platform teams as we finalize the procurement checklist:

1) We need the ability to keep customer-owned PII only in the US region for all inference outputs and logs. Is there an existing option to pin storage region per-tenant (not just control plane)?

2) We also need per-tenant TTL controls that can be configured at the project level (e.g., 30d / 90d / indefinite) and a guaranteed deletion flow that includes mTLS-backed transfer and KMS-delete. How mature is your retention configuration UI / API? Is this on your roadmap?

Attached is our retention checklist (PDF). Can your team confirm whether Redwood supports the items, and if not, whether there is a rough ETA?

Appreciate a straight yes/no + gaps list so we can close the security review.

Best,
Alicia Barnes
Head of Security Operations
Acme Corp

Attachments: acme-data-retention-checklist.pdf
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia.barnes@acme-corp.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-21T16:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on regional storage modes + configurable TTL for PII data

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front, then gaps and next steps below.

Yes:
- We can currently restrict inference outputs and KV cache persistence to specific cloud regions in Hosted mode for tenant-level routing (US-only option). That covers your primary ask for residency of outputs.

Partial / roadmap:
- Per-tenant persistent storage pinning for logs and long-term artifacts (audit logs, observability traces) is in progress (target: Q1 2027). Today those artifacts may traverse the control plane for observability unless you run Private.
- Configurable TTL at project level: we offer a defaults API and can set tenant-wide TTLs via support today, but a self-serve per-project UI/API is not yet GA. Roadmap to GA is Q1–Q2 2027 (we have a draft spec).

Deletion guarantees:
- KMS-integrated object deletion and HSM-backed key rotation are supported for Private deployments. For Hosted, we support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS for an enterprise plan, and we provide deletion hooks plus an audit log. A fully attested deletion workflow with KMS-delete callbacks is a product ask we are prioritizing for Dedicated/Private customers — ETA TBD (early 2027 planning).

Gaps summary (quick):
- Tenant-level UI for per-project TTLs (workaround: support-assisted config now)
- Native pinning of all observability artifacts to tenant region in Hosted (workaround: Dedicated/Private options)
- Certified KMS-delete attestation flow for Hosted (available in Private today)

Next steps I suggest:
1) I'll loop in Karthik to confirm technical constraints and propose a minimal matrix of storage modes + TTL semantics we can ship as an initial release.
2) Jonas — can you capture this as a small roadmap request (2–3 sprints) and flag any dependency on infra changes?

I'll attach a draft TTL/storage matrix for us to iterate on.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Data Controls
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-ttl-storage-modes-20261121.xlsx
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on regional storage modes + configurable TTL for PII data

Lauren, Jonas — digging into the engineering side; below are notes that map to the gaps Lauren listed plus a proposed minimal-scope implementation we can feasibly deliver in an initial milestone.

Current capabilities (technical):
- Request routing: tenant -> region mapping exists, handled by our smart router. No change needed to ensure inference compute and immediate token outputs stay in-region.
- KV/prefix cache: current cache shards are regional and can be pinned per-tenant (works today).
- Object store: audit logs and trace artifacts are emitted to a central observable stack (configurable, but defaults to multi-region); we can reconfigure to emit to a single US region for specific tenants with engineering changes.

Engineering constraints & risk:
- Making all observability artifacts region-pinned in Hosted requires changes to our logging aggregator and a per-tenant supplier configuration. Risk: medium (coordination with infra + logging vendor).
- Per-project TTL UI: low-risk product/infra work to expose TTL controls to the API and propagate to lifecycle policies on object stores.

Minimal-scope proposal (MVP) — target delivery in 6–10 weeks if prioritized:
1) Tenant-level storage mode flag (hosted): outputs-only vs outputs+artifacts. Defaults to outputs-only.
2) Tenant-level TTL API: set default TTL (30/90/never) that applies to generated artifacts and KV cache entries; TTL enforced by lifecycle jobs.
3) Deletion webhook + audit: immediate deletion request endpoint that triggers lifecycle purge and emits an audit event; KMS-delete integration reserved for Private/Dedicated initially.

Work needed: 2 backend engineers (4 weeks), 1 infra engineer (2 weeks), 1 frontend engineer (2–3 weeks) for the minimal admin UI and API docs.

Open questions for Lauren / Jonas:
- Do we need strict legal attestation language for Hosted deletion, or is operational confirmation + audit event sufficient for Acme to pass procurement?
- For Acme, do they expect TTL to apply retroactively to existing artifacts or only to new artifacts going forward? (This changes implementation complexity.)

I'll draft a tech spec once we confirm scope.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Serving Infra
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia.barnes@acme-corp.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-23T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on regional storage modes + configurable TTL for PII data

Alicia — thanks for the checklist and for the patience while we scoped this. Short summary for procurement/security:

- Residency: We can ensure inference outputs and KV cache persist only in the US region today for Hosted tenants.
- TTL: We can offer tenant-level TTL controls via an API and support-assisted configuration now. We propose a prioritized MVP to ship self-serve TTL controls and a tenant storage-mode flag within the next 6–10 weeks (details below). Retroactive TTL on historical artifacts is a separate opt-in migration; we can include it but will need a short runbook and ETA once you confirm.
- Deletion / KMS: For Hosted customers, KMS-delete attestation is currently available for Private deployments. For Hosted, we will provide an auditable deletion webhook and KMS envelope-support; full KMS-delete attestation is a planned follow-on.

Action items:
- Alicia / Acme: confirm whether TTL should apply retroactively to existing artifacts (reply to this thread).
- Acme: confirm target SLA for deletion acknowledgement (e.g., 24 hours vs 72 hours).
- Redwood: Lauren and Karthik will open a sprint-labeled roadmap ticket and share the tech spec by Nov 30. Jonas will track procurement dependencies.

I'll also share the Drive link to the draft TTL/storage matrix and the HubSpot deal.

Thanks — looking forward to closing the loop.

Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
